title: lnd admin REST API bound to 0.0.0.0 by the wireguard preset, protected by the firewall alone
summary: When lndconnect is enabled, the preset sets services.lnd.restAddress to 0.0.0.0. The macaroon-admin REST API listens on every interface, including the external one. The only protection is the nixos-fw default drop plus a single accept rule scoped to the wg interface and peer.
detail: The 2026-09-09 guards (firewall-must-be-enabled assertion, nftables refusal, -i wg-nb -s peer scoping) closed the silent-loss paths, but the bind itself remains. Residual risk: any other configuration that admits lnd.restPort through the firewall (allowedTCPPorts, a container port forward, a second interface rule) silently exposes the admin API on that network. The in-repo deferral doc explains why a naive rebind breaks six consumers and prescribes the safe variant: keep restAddress at 127.0.0.1 and add a second restlisten on the wg server address, with lnd ordered after wireguard-wg-nb.
recommendation: Implement the second-restlisten variant from docs/wireguard-rest-bind.md, including its pre-flight checklist (ordering, TLS SANs are not needed for the nocert path, cold-boot test asserting REST is not reachable on the external interface).

title: bitcoind RPC cookie is group-readable: every member of group bitcoin gets full privileged RPC
status: accepted by design, documented in code
summary: postStart chmods the .cookie to 0640 bitcoin:bitcoin. The operator user is placed in that group by default, so operator convenience and full wallet-capable RPC share one boundary.
detail: Carried from upstream audit finding L-10. The code comment documents the trade-off and directs new services to use an rpc user plus HMAC instead. The explicit 0640 does clear the other-read bit that a bare chmod g=r would leave to the daemon's umask.
recommendation: None required now. Keep group membership minimal and prefer the existing rpc-user pattern for any new consumer.

title: btcpayserver fetches price rates over clearnet, correlating invoice activity with the node IP
summary: Tor enforcement is deliberately disabled for btcpayserver because it cannot yet fetch rates over Tor. An observer of the rate providers can correlate invoice creation times with the node IP.
detail: Privacy-only impact, no fund or auth exposure. Flagged both in the preset and in examples/configuration.nix.
recommendation: Track upstream btcpayserver rate-fetch proxy support and re-enable enforcement when it lands.

title: netns-isolation service ids are not asserted unique
summary: Two services configured with the same id produce identical veth and interface names. The collision surfaces as broken netns setup, not as a silent security bypass.
detail: Misconfiguration robustness only. The option docs say ids must be unique, but nothing enforces it.
recommendation: Add an assertion comparing the id list for duplicates.

title: nix-bitcoin-wg-connect without an explicit host queries external-IP providers in clearnet
summary: The default QR generation path uses lndconnect's go-external-ip, which contacts a set of external IP providers. This reveals to those providers that this address runs an lndconnect-style node.
detail: Operator-invoked, interactive only. The docs show the explicit-host form that avoids it.
recommendation: None required. Operators who care can pass the host explicitly, as docs/services.md already shows.

title: The shared 'public' RPC user whitelist includes getpeerinfo and getnodeaddresses
summary: These two calls leak peer topology. They are kept because lnd's chain-backend health check and pruned block fetching require them, and this user is also the local services' RPC user.
detail: Only matters if an operator actually exposes this RPC user over a public proxy. The whitelist file itself tells that operator to narrow the list in their own config.
recommendation: None now. If the fork ever ships a public RPC proxy scenario, split the local and public users.

title: Flake example ships a plaintext demo login password
summary: The example node user is defined with password = "a" for VM convenience, with an in-file FIXME telling users to switch to hashedPassword or passwordFile.
detail: Template convenience for throwaway VMs. The FIXME already names the secure alternatives.
recommendation: None required. Could switch the template to initialPassword with a forced change, but the FIXME suffices.
